text:
Maya: Heads-up — ran into a subtle HF jinja -> Redwood prompt conversion bug that causes role propagation when a sentinel token is split across tokenizer boundaries. Repro below, pretty low-volume but dangerous for eval parity.

David: Ugh. Is this the same as the sentinel-preserve cases we've seen?

Maya: Related but different. In our case the HF chat_template emits a sentinel like `<|assistant|>` wrapped by whitespace and a punctuation char. With some tokenizers the sentinel gets split (e.g. `<|assist` + `ant|>`), and our RW preprocessor treats the second piece as plain content so the role marker doesn't get consumed -> role text bleeds into the next message.

Sophia: Can you paste a minimal repro?

Maya: Yep. Minimal template:
```jinja
{% for m in messages %}
- role: {{ m.role }}
  content: "{{ m.content }}"
{% endfor %}
```
And messages payload: `[{"role":"assistant","content":"Thanks! <|assistant|> Next: confirm."}]`

Leo: So the model sees `assistant` token twice? That would change logits after quantization too.

Maya: Exactly. On FP32 run with tokenizer A we get correct strip, but with tokenizer B (which uses byte-level split) the sentinel becomes two tokens and our converter code only strips whole sentinel strings. We observed a small but consistent drop in ROUGE on our instruction evals after quantizing model with tokenizer B.

David: Any quick fix ideas? Patch the converter to run tokenizer-level normalization instead of naive string replace?

Maya: Proposed short-term patch: run the rendered prompt through the target tokenizer and then remove token sequences that match the sentinel tokenization pattern before detokenizing. Pseudo-command: `python tools/normalize_sentinels.py --tokenizer hf/xxx --input rendered_prompt.txt` — this collapses sentinel token fragments.

Sophia: Long term we should: 1) record tokenizer tokenization fingerprints in model card; 2) add a CI check on HF->RW conversion that compares detokenized->redwood-prompt back to original intent.

Maya: Agree. I added a tiny harness: `tools/compare_tokenizers.py --model hf:my-model --template tests/sentinel-repro.json` that prints tokenization diffs and a delta score. Ran it in CI locally and attached logs.

deploy-bot: test run complete — 1965432310 — sentinel-repro passed on tokenizer A, failed on tokenizer B (diff > 0.01).

Leo: Can you drop the failing tokenization diff output here?

Maya: Pasted snippet: `orig: "<|assistant|>" -> tokens: ["<|assist", "ant|>"]` vs `hf-tokenizer: ["<|assistant|>"]`. Our naive `replace("<|assistant|>", "")` only matched latter.

David: Good find. For the immediate release branch can you add a small function that runs `tokenizer.encode(sentinel)` and then replaces those token sequences (reconstructed via tokenizer.decode) in the rendered prompt? Keep it opt-in behind a flag.

Maya: Yep — I'll open a PR to add `--normalize-sentinels` to `redwood-convert`. Also adding a regression test that quantizes with 4-bit config and runs the eval prompt and checks the response header doesn't start with `assistant:` bleed.

Sophia: Small note: update model `config.json` check too. Some HF config variants set `bos_token` differently which interacts with sentinel matching. Add that to the tokenizer parity report.

Leo: Thx. Also log this in the model onboarding checklist — add `tokenizer parity` and `sentinel-split` checks under tokenization section.

Maya: Will do. Filing a follow-up ticket in GH with repro and suggested patches. Ping @eng-ml for review when PR is up. :+1:
